questions.q: Why doesn't core Apache Airflow (`pip install apache-airflow`) include Snowflake, Postgres, or S3 support built in?
options: Bundling every possible integration would make the core package enormous and force everyone to install dependencies they don't need
Those systems don't support Python
Airflow's license forbids including third-party integrations
Integrations are only available in Airflow's paid tier
questions.explain: Integrations ship as separate, independently-versioned provider packages so users install only what they need.

questions.q: What four things does a provider package typically bundle for one system?
options: Hooks, Operators, Sensors, and a connection type
A new scheduler, a new webserver, a new database, and a new UI
Only documentation — no runnable code
A DAG template and nothing else
questions.explain: A provider package is a coherent bundle: the low-level Hook, task-shaped Operators, Sensors, and the connection type that appears in the Add Connection form.

questions.q: How do you install support for a new system, like Snowflake?
options: pip install apache-airflow-providers-snowflake, then restart so it's discovered
Edit airflow.cfg and manually list every class name
Write a custom plugin from scratch — providers cannot be installed via pip
Providers are always pre-installed and cannot be added or removed
questions.explain: Provider packages install like any Python package, and Airflow auto-discovers them at startup via entry points.

questions.q: What does an import path like `airflow.providers.snowflake.hooks.snowflake` tell you?
options: This code comes from a provider package (apache-airflow-providers-snowflake), not core Airflow
This is a deprecated, unsupported code path
The class was written by the DAG author, not Apache Airflow
This code only works in Airflow's test environment
questions.explain: The airflow.providers.* prefix always signals provider-package code — if the import fails, the fix is usually installing that provider.

questions.q: Where can you check which provider packages are currently installed and their versions, inside the Airflow UI?
options: Admin > Providers
Browse > Task Instances
Home > Dashboard
Docs > REST API Reference
questions.explain: The Admin > Providers page lists every installed provider package along with its version, useful for confirming installs or debugging import errors.
